messages.author: 25ddb7cda687795b
messages.subject: trouble with unit arithmetics
parts:
Hi all,

I am having trouble setting the margin using unit arithmetics. What am
I missing?


Example:

#+begin_src R
library("ggplot2")
library("grid")

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(displ, hwy)) + geom_point()

margin1 <-
unit(c(0.5, 1, 0.5, 1),
c("lines", "lines", "lines", "strwidth"),
data=list(NULL, NULL, NULL, "uplrp"))

margin2 <-
unit(c(0, 0, 0, 1),
c("lines", "lines", "lines", "strwidth"),
data=list(NULL, NULL, NULL, "1.00"))

margin3 <- margin1-margin2

margin3 ## valid

p + theme(plot.margin=margin1) ## works
p + theme(plot.margin=margin2) ## works
p + theme(plot.margin=margin3) ## does not work
#+end_src

Regards,
Andreas

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: trouble with unit arithmetics
parts:
Hi,

unit.arithmetic objects have quite a few bugs (try str(margin3) for instance); you could try to convert it to an absolute size with

margin4 = convertUnit(margin3, "mm")

though it is not exactly ideal.

HTH,

baptiste

parts: Hi,

On 12 March 2013 23:13, Andreas Leha <andrea...@med.uni-goettingen.de> wrote:

<baptist...@gmail.com> writes:

> instance); you could try to convert it to an absolute size with
>
> margin4 = convertUnit(margin3, "mm")

Thanks a lot for this.  It works nicely in my application.

>
> though it is not exactly ideal.

Could you elaborate on this?  What makes it "not exactly ideal"?

Well, for a start convertUnits needs to have a device open to do its calculations, sometimes resulting in an additional blank page when working non-interactively.
 
Also, on top of my head the conversion of units has to make some assumptions that may not be as general as one would like: it can convert the lineheight to say mm, only assuming a given fontsize, but the user may have set it differently in his/her own viewport. Similarly, calculations are frozen after the conversion, so resizing the plot window will break your layout, etc.

But at the end of the day, it can do the job. 

Cheers,

b.

PS: It would be good to report both bugs to grid and ggplot2 package maintainers, by the way.

>
> HTH,

It did indeed.

Regards,
Andreas
